question.text: Under Section 135(5) of the Companies Act 2013 and its Rules, a company liable to CSR is required to spend at least:

answer.text: 1% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 2 financial years
2% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 3 financial years; projects of INR 1 crore or more mandatorily require impact assessment
2.5% of net profit of the current financial year only
5% of turnover of the immediately preceding financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135(5) mandates CSR spend of at least 2% of the average net profit of the 3 immediately preceding financial years. The Companies (CSR Policy) Amendment Rules 2021 mandate impact assessment, through an independent agency, for CSR projects outlay of INR 1 crore or more (and the company has average CSR obligation of INR 10 crore or more). The Trap: Option A understates the rate and uses 2-year average; option C uses 2.5% (a fabrication) and wrong base-year; option D uses turnover base (wrong — CSR is net-profit-based, not turnover-based). Cross-Exam Context: V-A / X-A (MF Distributor / IA) test donor-side 80G; XXIII tests the corporate CSR trigger + impact-assessment linkage which flows directly into SE engagement demand. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Impact assessment under Rule 8(3) is where the SIA's work interfaces with the Companies Act — your engagement letter should cite both the SEBI ICDR framework (if SSE) AND Rule 8(3) (if CSR-funded project ≥ INR 1 cr). Dual citation locks in the fee basis.
